judgments.catchwords: Originating Summons for declaratory relief as to the true construction of the Last Will and Testament - testator’s intention as expressed in the words of the will read as a whole, and not his unexpressed subjective wishes - Second, the court will, so far as the language permits, prefer a construction that gives every clause some operative effect over one that renders any clause meaningless - where two constructions are reasonably open, and one produces an intestacy, be it whole or partial, while the other avoids it, the court prefers the construction that avoids intestacy - the court is not entitled to make a fresh will for the testator merely because it suspects that he did not mean what he plainly said - the court may inform itself of the testator’s actual circumstances at the time he made the will, this includes his family, his property, and his business relationships, to understand what he meant by the words he used, before concluding that those words are ambiguous or deciding how any ambiguity is to be resolved. - company is a legal person distinct from its members, and that a shareholder, even one holding practically the whole of the issued capital, has no legal or equitable proprietary interest in the company’s assets.

judgments.title: Pendakwa Raya & ors v Julasiri Bin Akilmara
judgments.catchwords: Offence under section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 read together with section 34 of the Penal Code - Whether the trial judge should have informed at the close of the prosecution's case, that the defence was being called upon to answer a case of actual trafficking or presumed trafficking? - Overwhelming evidence proved the elements of custody, control, and knowledge - Actual possession of the impugned drugs was established - Section 180 (1) and (4) of the Criminal Procedure Code - Procedure after conclusion of case for prosecution - No statutory or legal requirement to state the presumption when calling for the defence - Formal verbal label for an evidentiary rule at the close of the prosecution's case is unnecessary - Statutory presumption of trafficking under section 37(da)(xvi) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 - Section 422 of the Criminal Procedure Code - Not vitiate the conviction - No miscarriage of justice - Failure either to make or to record such a finding does not ipso facto - The law does not require a mini-judgment or detailed legal reasons at the close of the prosecution’s case
